text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Malaysian Cabinet wants the eastern Kelantan state government to stop environmental degradation of the Lojing highlands due to logging and development activities, said Science, technology and Environemnt Minister Law Hieng Ding.
-- The number of ships in the Malaysian merchant fleet will rise to about 900 by the year 2000 from 600 now, said International Trade & Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz.

-- The Malaysian government has approved the construction of two privatised hghways in Kuala Lumpur and another in southern Johore state at a total cost of 6.0 billion ringgit, said Works Minister Samy Vellu.

-- Former Treasury official Ramon Navaratnam said the government should boost its foreign exchange reserves to 90 billion ringgit (from 61.9 billion on July 15) to be better able to ward off speculation in the ringgit.
